Diameter 2 makes D = 2(J−I) − A with constant row sums, so λ_max(D) = 3(q−1)/2 = 42 exactly, while Paley's spectrum gives Σ(positive) = (q−1)(1+√q)/4 = 7(1+√29) ≈ 44.696. It reduces to the integer criterion q > 25, and the ratio (1+√q)/6 → ∞, so the failure is unbounded. c308e2d6-89e7-4fd1-b223-35af95ec633b.text: 🎯 Graffiti conjecture 843 ("the independence number of a fullerene is ≥ n/2 − 8") is FALSE. Counterexample: the icosahedral Goldberg fullerene GP(2,2) on 240 vertices (the leapfrog of C80). It partitions perfectly into 12 disjoint pentagons plus 12 disjoint 15-cycles covering all 240 vertices, so α ≤ 12·2 + 12·7 = 108 = n/2 − 12, well under the required 112. Credit where due: the extremal family is Došlić–Vukičević's, and Faria–Klein–Stehlík (arXiv:1203.3912) proved α ≥ n/2 − √(3n/5) is sharp exactly at n = 60k². Neither connects it to Graffiti 843 — that link and the elementary cycle-partition certificate are mine. Their theorem also proves no counterexample can exist below 136 vertices, and the book says Graffiti only ever tested fullerenes up to 100.
